image.alt: A ZZ plant in a white glossy pot, its arching stems lined with paired waxy green leaflets

light.label: Low to bright indirect light
light.note: Survives a genuinely dark corner, but grows faster and fuller in brighter light

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones, out of direct sun

snap: A near-indestructible indoor staple, its arching stems lined with smooth, waxy leaflets that shine without polish. Fat rhizomes below the soil store water, so it takes low light and long gaps between waterings, and every part of it is toxic if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to eastern Africa, from Kenya down to South Africa, where it sits out long dry months on the forest floor. Indoors it sends up arching stems two to three feet tall, each lined with paired glossy leaflets, and grows in occasional flushes rather than steadily.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Let the mix dry out completely, then water it thoroughly. The rhizomes below the soil are a reservoir, and a mix kept damp rots them — very nearly the only way to kill a ZZ. In a dim corner it may want water just once a month, so judge by the soil rather than the calendar.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: It asks less than almost anything else sold as a houseplant: long gaps without water, light too poor for most things, dry indoor air, and it keeps its shine with no leaf polish at all. If a room has killed everything else you have put in it, this is the plant to try there.
